title: One more killed in elephant attack in Hassan’s Belur taluk; protests intensify

ai.summary: Residents of Belur taluk in Hassan district protested after a second death in human-elephant conflict, blaming forest department negligence and demanding the minister visit for a permanent solution.

facts.claim: Another person died in an elephant attack in Nagenahalli in Belur taluk
facts.quote: Less than 48 hours after a woman was killed in an elephant attack at Chowdanahalli in Belur taluk, another person died in a similar incident at Nagenahalli in the taluk on Monday (November 16).

facts.claim: Hafees-Ur-Rahman, 60, was trampled to death by an elephant while on his way to a coffee estate
facts.quote: Hafees-Ur-Rahman, 60, was on his way to the coffee estate where he worked when he encountered an elephant, which trampled him to death.

facts.claim: Residents staged protests after the first death, blaming forest department negligence
facts.quote: Following the death of Jayamma, 65, at Chowdahalli on Saturday (November 14) evening, people of Belur taluk staged a protest on Sunday (November 15) with the body. They blamed the Forest Department’s negligence for the series of deaths due to human-elephant conflict in the region.

facts.claim: The Forest Department deployed an Elephant Task Force to monitor elephant movements
facts.quote: The Forest Department has deployed an Elephant Task Force that monitors the movement of elephants in the region.

facts.claim: Nearly 100 people have died in elephant attacks over the last 10 years in Belur, Sakaleshpur and Alur taluks
facts.quote: Nearly 100 people have died in elephant attacks over the last 10 years.

facts.claim: Residents of Nagenahalli said there was no alert about elephant movement
facts.quote: According to residents of Nagenahalli, there was no alert, particularly about the movement of elephants near their place.

ai.background_note: Human-elephant conflict in Belur taluk has led to repeated deaths and protests, with the Forest Department deploying an Elephant Task Force but residents claiming inadequate alerts and negligence.
